Siri AI is a major upgrade for the Apple assistant, now available on iOS 27. I noticed a standout difference between it and other AI assistants, and it's a good difference.

The all-new Siri on iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, unlike other AI chatbots

Since the first beta of iOS 27 launched, I've been using Siri AI for nearly four months. Overall, it has met all my expectations.

The new Siri is far more powerful than its predecessor, truly delivering on its original promise as a genuinely helpful assistant on Apple devices.

However, I have to admit: if you need the most advanced, most powerful AI tools on the market, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini may be a better fit for you.

That said, after using Siri AI and then comparing it with those third-party tools, I noticed a key difference that makes me lean明显傾向 Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't go on at length, nor does it mimic human-like personalities that lead you to unknowingly build a personal relationship with it.

Siri is practical, smart, and flexible, doing what you ask it to do. But the way it responds clearly shows it's a tool, not a person. It often reminds you it's an AI and can make mistakes. It also doesn't pretend to go on dates with you.

By contrast, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are all full of personality and opinions, displaying more human-like traits, but to me that feeling doesn't feel authentic.

I know some users like this more 'humanised' approach. But I'd rather have AI assistants stick to doing their job properly and stop pretending to be something they're not.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. Apple understands this and has built the all-new Siri on that foundation, which I really appreciate.

What do you think about how 'human-like' AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
